steps.description:
Your Robot has 2 important parts:

  • The Raspberry Pi, which is the computer or the brain.
  • The Grove Hat, which is a special layer with places to connect sensors and modules.

     

You'll be using a Raspberry Pi robot for output. You can choose to use a physical robot or the virtual robot when testing your code.

When you power up your robot, it will appear on the robot list within a minute.

An LCD is a module for displaying text.

A Buzzer is for playing sounds.

You can use either the Note block or the Tone block to play a sound.

Study with the code below and experiment with it.



Form the a code that makes a blinking text and beeping sound together for 10 times (the text and sound should appear and disappear together).









-

There are different ways to make text and sound appear together.

Below shows two examples. Try them out.

    

Play a sound continuously for 3 seconds.

While the sound is playing, show a text blinking 3 times.






-

You can interact with the robot by pressing buttons.

    

The Button block continuously sends back a value 0 when not pressed and a value 1 when pressed.

Below shows how you can form the condition to detect button press with an If block.

    

An If block only runs once. You can use a Forever loop to keep the programming running.


Form the following code simulating a light switch:

  1. When Button D18 is pressed, display "lights on". It should stay there even when the button is released.
  2. When Button D24 is pressed, display "lights off". It should stay there even when the button is released.







-

A Repat Until loop repeats a set of codes until a condition is True.

A Repeat While loop repeats a set of codes while a condition is True.

Below shows two sets of codes that have the same output.

    


A Wait Until block is also similar to a Repeat Until block. It waits for a condition to be True before moving on to the next block.

   


Form a code that simulates a charging station as follow:

  1. Display "Hold Button D22 to charge" until Button D22 is pressed. Show the text in two rows as it is long.
  2. When the button is pressed and held on, display "Charging" with a beeping sound until the button is released.
  3. When the button is released, display "Charging done" for 2 seconds and end the program.







-

An Ultrasonic sensor is used to detect obstacle in front of it. It returns the distance in centimetres (cm).


The AND operator is used to check if two conditions are True. When both conditions are True, the AND block will be True. Otherwise, it will be False.

     


You can switch between two display styles as follow (it does not affect the logic).

    

Below shows how you can use the AND block to detect range. 

    


Study the diagram below carefully, write a code to detect the parcels as follows:

  1. Display "parcel detected" when a parcel of height within 20cm to 30cm passes under the ultrasonic sensor.
  2. Display "oversize item" when a parcel's height is beyond 30cm.
  3. Otherwise, display "no parcel".
   









-

A Colour sensor is used to detect colour. Regardless of whether there is any object in front of it, it will constantly return one of these five values: Red, Green, Blue, Orange or White.


You can form a condition to check whether the Colour sensor is detecting a certain colour as shown:

The OR operator is used to check if at least one of two conditions is True.


Create a colour detector using the Colour sensor as follows:

  1. Red and orange are warms colours. Green and blue are cool colours.
  2. If a warm colour is detected, display "warm colour".
  3. If a cool colour is detected, display "cool colour".
  4. If neither warm nor cool colour is detected, display "neutral colour".









-

You have a car that is equipped with a Color sensor underneath and an Ultrasonic sensor in front.

Below is the code to control car but the control is malfunctioning.

Fix the bug and enhance the code (you can add more blocks) to include the following features:

  1. Controls the car with buttons:
    D22 - Turn left     
    D24 - Turn right     
    D22+D24 - Move forward
  2. Stops the car if an obstacle is within 50 cm.
  3. The forward speed should be 100 by default but it should slow down to 50 when travelling within a school zone (the road of a school zone is painted red).
